feature: One copy hands off the picture and its spec list
summary: Copy Image now puts the spec list on the clipboard as text beside the picture whenever the document has a visible measurement. Paste into a document or chat and the picture lands; paste into a plain text field and the list lands. Before, that took Copy Image and then Copy as Spec List.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, flag Measurements panel on. Open any screenshot and drop two measurements on it with the Measure tool (press i).

try.do: Press Shift-Command-C. A pill at the bottom of the canvas should read Copied, Image and spec list with 2 measurements.
Paste into a TextEdit rich text document or a Notes note. The picture should land, with no text under it.
Paste into Spotlight, a Safari address bar or Terminal. The two-line spec list should land.
Paste into a Mail compose window. Expect the picture.
Paste into Messages, then into Slack or Discord. Note which of them pastes the picture and which pastes the list.
Turn both measurements off with their eyes, press Shift-Command-C again, and paste into Terminal. Nothing should land, because the list would only be a header.
Open a screenshot with no measurements and press Shift-Command-C. The pill should read Copied, Image, and the clipboard is the picture alone.

evaluate: Did every chat client you tried paste the picture? If one pasted the list instead, that is the case where this change should be withdrawn.
Does the pill line, Image and spec list with 2 measurements, tell you what you will get when you paste, or is it too much to read in a glance?
Would you rather the list travel with the picture even when it is only the header line?
Does one Copy Image feel like enough of a hand-off, or do you still reach for Copy as Spec List?
rough: Messages, Slack and Discord were not tried by a person this session: the agent has no permission to drive other apps, so the chat-client check the task called for is yours to make in step 5. The equivalents that could be probed (rich NSTextView, a WebKit editable field, plain text fields) all behaved as intended.
A rich text view that does not accept graphics falls through to the list, which is what a paste has to do there, but it may surprise in an app that shows formatted text yet no images.
Copy Image showed no confirmation at all before; the pill is new for it. If it feels like noise for a picture-only copy, the picture-only case could stay silent.
